confidence_boundary: The source identities and result index are confirmed from executable and previously committed runtime evidence. The target-mode names and fail-closed rules are the System 2.0 resolver contract derived from those confirmed sources; they are not claims that the original game already has a generic effect-target dispatcher.

confirmed_result_fields.lifetime: Valid while the battle-result controller and its battle object at +0x38 remain live.
confirmed_result_fields.meaning: winning combatant record index; -1 means unresolved or no normal winner, 0 and 1 select the two 20-byte combatant records
mutations: 0x02241A64..0x02241A74 resolves a direct result to index 0 or 1.
0x02242094..0x0224209C calls result helper 0x02244440 and stores its 0-or-1 return value.
confirmed_result_fields.reset: A new battle-result controller reconstructs the field as -1; destructor 0x0223E450 destroys the associated battle object and ends validity.

confirmed_result_fields.initialization: Constructor 0x0223E238 initializes the byte to zero, but it has no loser meaning until a valid winner has been resolved.
confirmed_result_fields.lifetime: Presentation cache used after winner resolution during the live result-controller lifetime.
confirmed_result_fields.meaning: cached losing combatant record index, written as the opposite of winner index 0 or 1
mutations: 0x02241CD4..0x02241CE4 stores 1 when winner is 0 and 0 otherwise.
confirmed_result_fields.reset: Reinitialized by the next result-controller constructor and discarded at destruction.

instruction_evidence.purpose: construct the result controller, initialize +0x21 to -1, and construct/store the linked battle object at +0x38
resolve a direct battle result and store winning combatant index 0 or 1 at result-controller +0x21
call the calculated-result helper, store its 0-or-1 return at +0x21, then reject -1 before normal result processing
read +0x21 and select winner combatant record 0 or 1 for result presentation
derive the opposite loser index and select the losing combatant record for presentation
guard unresolved -1 and compare the winning combatant with the active player-side participant before reward processing
consume the same signed winner index during final result and progression handling
calculated battle-result helper; evaluates both combatant records and returns only index 0 or 1
destroy the linked battle object and end result-context validity

resolver_context.challenger_participant: Resolve session +0x28E to its 20-byte descriptor, then read the low nibble of descriptor byte +0x0F.
resolver_context.defender_participant: Resolve session +0x28D to its 20-byte descriptor, then read the low nibble of descriptor byte +0x0F.
resolver_context.is_ai: Read participant +0xC8 and test for non-null.
resolver_context.source_participant: An explicit participant index supplied by the effect-dispatch call; it must never be inferred from record order.
resolver_context.winner_record_index: Read signed result-controller +0x21 only after the result-settled timing point.

target_modes.resolution: Return the single participant index stored at battle object +0x06. A combatant-only effect must separately require that this participant maps to one of the two current combatant records.

target_modes.availability: available for a distinct two-combatant collision
target_modes.resolution: Return the participant selected by session +0x28D.

target_modes.resolution: Return the participant selected by session +0x28E.
Return source_participant unchanged after confirming that it is one of the live combatants for combatant-only effects.

target_modes.availability: requires a distinct combatant pair and an explicit source participant that matches exactly one combatant
target_modes.resolution: Return the other combatant participant. Do not interpret Gate ownership, human/AI identity, or record number as the source.

target_modes.availability: available for a distinct two-combatant collision
target_modes.resolution: Return the ordered unique pair [defender_participant, challenger_participant].

target_modes.availability: available only after result-controller +0x21 is 0 or 1
target_modes.resolution: Map winner record index 0 to defender participant and index 1 to challenger participant.

target_modes.resolution: Map winner record index 0 to challenger participant and index 1 to defender participant. Derive this as winner_index XOR 1 rather than trusting result-controller +0x0E before its presentation write.

target_modes.availability: available while participant objects and both combatants are live
target_modes.resolution: Filter the ordered unique combatant pair to participants whose +0xC8 pointer is null.

target_modes.availability: available while participant objects and both combatants are live
target_modes.resolution: Filter the ordered unique combatant pair to participants whose +0xC8 pointer is non-null.

fail_closed_rules: Reject winner and loser targets while result-controller +0x21 is -1 or outside 0..1.
Reject opponent, both, winner, and loser targeting when defender and challenger do not form a distinct two-combatant pair.
Reject self or opponent targeting when no explicit source participant was supplied.
Reject opponent targeting when the source participant is not exactly one of the two live combatants.
Do not silently convert an owner participant who is not currently battling into defender, challenger, or opponent.
Deduplicate human and AI target sets by participant index while preserving defender-then-challenger order.
Do not persist participant pointers, battle pointers, result-controller pointers, or AI-controller pointers in Gate data.
supported_conclusions: Gate owner, defender, challenger, human, and AI targets derive from independent confirmed sources.
The winner index is a signed result-controller field, not a battle-object field and not a participant index.
Winner and loser participant identities require one additional combatant-index-to-participant mapping step.
The generic self and opponent modes must be relative to an explicit effect source, not relative to Gate ownership or player/AI identity.
The original game does not provide a generic target-mode dispatcher; the listed modes are a deterministic System 2.0 contract over confirmed runtime context.
